entry_conditions: Enter after the red block has been unstacked and is being carried, or partway through the descent/release transition. Supported states include red high in the gripper near index 190-240 and red near the red pad with fingers still closed near index 260-280. The policy uses only causal observations: qpos finger aperture, qvel finger motion, TCP pose, red pose, blue pose, and fixed goal positions in the world frame.
exit_conditions: Exit after red_pose is near the red goal at tabletop height, finger aperture has opened for release, and TCP has retreated upward/away from red; if the next policy expects blue acquisition, this policy can continue through the overlap until the TCP has approached blue, closed on it, and blue_pose is lifted by about index 500-520.
overlap_role: The expanded slice intentionally covers the shared transition from red release to blue acquisition. This implementation treats the overlap as a learned reset and object-switch phase, not as an instantaneous cut: red remains stable at the red goal while the arm retreats with open fingers, travels to blue, closes, and lifts blue.
successor_readiness: A successor should receive a state in which red is no longer moving with the gripper, red is on or very near the red pad, and the gripper/TCP are available for blue. For a blue-acquisition successor, readiness is improved when the observation also shows TCP near blue or blue already lifted with closed fingers. A geometric red-at-goal state alone is not sufficient if fingers are still closed around red and the TCP has not started the release/retreat transition.
failure_signatures: Warning signs are opening high above the table, retreating horizontally while qpos fingers remain closed on red, red_pose changing with the gripper after the supposed release, fingers failing to open before the blue approach, or blue contact/closure occurring before red is stable at its pad. The demonstrations do not prove recovery from red dropped outside the pad.
continuation_guidance: Continue this policy if the current observation is within the release/reset overlap: red is at the red goal but the hand is still close to it, or the hand has just opened and is retreating toward blue. Transfer earlier only if the successor can handle an open gripper still above red. Continue to the end of the overlap when a successor requires a blue-lift entry state rather than just a released-red reset.
limitations: Observed support is from state/action demonstrations without contact force measurements. Finger aperture and object/TCP relative motion are used as inferred release cues; they are not hard safety predicates. The learned model uses joint-space action diffusion and does not implement IK, collision constraints, or force-controlled release.
